findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews overdue notice counts on the first of every month. Historical figures are archived for five years before being summarized and retired."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph, or replace it with circulation data that actually supports the argument (e.g., trend data on overdue notice volume over time).
findings.violation: This is irrelevant to the recommendation to end overdue fines; it describes an administrative archiving schedule with no bearing on whether fines should be eliminated.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews self-checkout usage at the end of each quarter. Branch-level totals roll up into the consortium's shared reporting dashboard."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph or explain explicitly how self-checkout usage relates to the fines decision if a connection exists.
findings.violation: Self-checkout usage has no stated connection to fines, return rates, or the recommendation being made; it is a non-sequitur under a heading that should motivate the proposal.

findings.evidence: "the on-time-or-eventual return rate for borrowed items held at 93 percent"
findings.fix: Report on-time return rate and eventual (including late) return rate as separate figures so the timeliness effect of removing fines is visible.
findings.violation: Combining "on-time" and "eventual" returns into one metric obscures whether removing fines caused items to be returned later (just not lost), which is the actual concern a reader would have about ending fines.

findings.evidence: "The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot."
findings.fix: Either administer the survey at the 18-month pilot conclusion and report that figure, or explicitly note that the 12-month reading is a midpoint snapshot and justify why it's being used as the "after" measure.
findings.violation: The pilot lasted 18 months but the "after" survey was taken at the 12-month mark, so the before/after comparison doesn't actually span the full pilot period being cited as evidence.

findings.evidence: "the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches"
findings.fix: Either present data/reasoning showing the non-pilot branches are comparable to the pilot branches, or scope the recommendation's confidence level accordingly.
findings.violation: The pilot data covers only 5 of the 10 branches; the document gives no evidence or reasoning for why the result should generalize to the other 5 branches, which may differ in patron demographics or usage patterns.

findings.evidence: "eliminates overdue fines for all item types at all ten branches"
findings.fix: Note whether the pilot tracked item-type-specific return rates, and either justify the all-item-types scope with that data or limit the recommendation to the item types actually tested.
findings.violation: The pilot's return-rate results are not broken down by item type, so extending the change to "all item types" is unsupported by the data presented.

findings.evidence: "matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established"
findings.fix: Either cite the specific pilot data showing a 60-day return pattern, or remove the claim that the pilot established this threshold and justify the 60-day cutoff on other grounds.
findings.violation: No 60-day return window or related threshold appears anywhere in the "What the Pilot Showed" section, so this claim that the pilot data established this pattern is unsupported and appears fabricated.

findings.evidence: "The systems team plans to update the online catalog's fine-display field during the same rollout window."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence or replace the section with actual evidence/reasoning for systemwide applicability (e.g., comparability of branches, consistency of effect across pilot sites).
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, first line
findings.violation: This sentence is irrelevant to the heading's claim and provides no reasoning for why the pilot result should generalize systemwide.

findings.evidence: "This is simply how patron behavior works, and no library that has tried it has ever found otherwise."
findings.fix: Remove the claim or replace it with cited evidence from comparable libraries/studies that have implemented fine elimination.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, second line
findings.violation: This is an unsupported, sweeping generalization with no citation or evidence, presented as self-evident fact to justify systemwide rollout.

findings.evidence: "The branch renovation project remains on schedule for completion next spring."
findings.fix: Remove the irrelevant renovation detail and add an actual response to the funding shortfall (e.g., alternative funding source, cost-benefit comparison, or data from the pilot on net financial impact).
findings.location: "Addressing the Revenue Concern" section, final line
findings.violation: This sentence does not address the skeptic's point about lost materials-replacement funding at all; the section heading promises a rebuttal to the revenue concern but none is given.
